facts.text: I am thinking of writing a play and I am stuck on the structure.
I have been listening to musical soundtracks a lot lately.
I have been listening to the Hamilton soundtrack nonstop.
I watched the recorded version of Hamilton on Disney+ a few weeks back.
I am interested in writing a play that explores the complexities of family dynamics and relationships.
I am interested in Arthur Miller's plays that focus on the American Dream and the flaws in the idea of perfection.
I want to explore how past experiences shape people and affect their current relationships.
I have been inspired by The Glass Menagerie by Tennessee Williams.
I want to read more plays that use non-linear storytelling.
I want to read more plays that explore the power of memory and nostalgia.
I am thinking of using a non-linear structure to explore the complexities of my characters' relationships.
I want to jump back and forth between different moments in my characters' past.
I want to use memory to reveal character backstory and motivations.
I am considering using memory in a way similar to Tennessee Williams in The Glass Menagerie.
I am thinking of using a combination of scene headings, lighting, and sound cues to guide the audience through a non-linear narrative.
I want to create a sense of fluidity between the past and present in my play.
I want to use transitions that blur the lines between different time periods.
I might use a fade-to-black to signal a jump in time.
I might use a sudden shift in lighting to signal a jump in time.
I want to use sound cues such as music or sound effects to evoke nostalgia or create continuity between scenes.
I want each flashback or memory in my play to serve a purpose in revealing character insights or deepening relationships.
I do not want flashbacks to feel like gratuitous additions.
I want to vary the pace and tone of scenes to create a sense of flow and emotional resonance.
